sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:-
"...to issue a Writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus filed against the action of respondent No. 5 in interfering into life and liberty of the petitioner and calling the petitioner to the police station and detaining him and interfering into civil dispute between petitioner and respondent No.6 by the influence of respondent No. 7 and creating panic situation is illegal and arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India and also violative of Principle of Natural justice and consequently to direct the respondent No. 5 not to interfere with the peaceful life and liberty of the petitioner and not to threaten the petitioner to handover the petitioner house to respondent Nos. 6 and 7 which is situated at Halia Village and Mandal Nalgonda District..."
2. The petitioner claims to be working as private employee in VNR Vignana Jyothi Institute of Engineering Technology College and the petitioner and husband of respondent No.6 are own brothers.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that the husband of respondent No.6 was expired CVBR, J Wp_31799_2023 in the year 2011, thereafter disputes arose between petitioner and respondent No.6 for partition of the ancestral property.

It is the further case of the petitioner that respondent No.6, instead of approaching the competent civil Court to resolve the family disputes for partition of the ancestral properties, lodged a complaint before respondent No.5 and as the said complaint revealed cognizable offence, the police registered a case in Crime No.140 of 2019 dated 10.06.2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of I.P.C.
It is the further case of the petitioner that at the instance of elders and well wishers of the family, the matter has been referred to Lok Adalath and settled.

The grievance of the petitioner is that even after the matter being settled before Lok Adalat, at the instance of respondent Nos.6 and 7, respondent No.5 is interfering with the civil disputes and frequently summoning him to the police station and confining him for hours together and forcing him to enter into a settlement with respondent Nos.6 and 7.
CVBR, J Wp_31799_2023 3.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has vehemently contended that respondent No.5 is not having any power or authority to intervene into the civil disputes pending between the petitioner and respondent Nos.6 and 7 and to force him to enter into the settlement.
It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the above action of respondent No.5 amounts to violation of the rights guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 5, on instructions, would submit that the respondents-police are not interfering into the civil disputes pending between the petitioner and respondent Nos.6 and 7 and infact a case in Crime No.140 of 2019 was registered against the petitioner and the same was settled in Lok Adalat in terms of the compromise entered by the parties and thereafter, the respondents- police never interfered with the civil disputes nor summoned the petitioner to the police station.

In view of the said submissions, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition directing respondent No.5 not to interfere with the civil disputes pending between the petitioner and respondent No.6 and 7 in any manner and if the presence of either of the parties is required for the purpose of investigation in any crime, respondent No.5 is directed to follow the procedure as contemplated in law.
6. With the above observations, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
7. As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
